q: Which of the following compounds is a saturated hydrocarbon?
qs.e: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds (C–C and C–H) and have the general formula C n H 2n+2 for alkanes or C n H 2n for cycloalkanes. Cyclohexane (C 6 H 12) is a cycloalkane with only single bonds, making it saturated. Propene (C 3 H 6) has a C=C double bond, so it is unsaturated. Propyne (C 3 H 4) has a C≡C triple bond, making it unsaturated. Benzene (C 6 H 6) has delocalized π-electrons in its aromatic ring, so it is unsaturated. qs.tag: RRB JE 27 May 2019 Shift 3 CBT 1
q: Which of the following is used as a fuel in cars along with petrol?
qs.e: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is commonly blended with petrol as a fuel additive in cars, typically in mixtures like E10 (10% ethanol, 90% petrol) or E85 (85% ethanol, 15% petrol). This blend improves combustion efficiency and reduces emissions of harmful pollutants like carbon monoxide (CO) and unburnt hydrocarbons. Ethanol is a renewable biofuel produced by fermentation of sugars from crops like sugarcane or corn. Methane (CH₄) is primarily used as natural gas for heating and cooking, not as a mainstream automotive fuel blend. Butane (C₄H₁₀) is used in LPG for cooking and as a propellant. Ethane (C₂H₆) is mainly a feedstock for ethylene production in petrochemical industries, not used as a fuel in cars.

qs.tag: RRB Technician Grade III 09/03/2026 4:30 PM - 6:00 PM
q: Which of the following is the product formed when ethene (C 2 H 4) reacts with hydrogen (H 2) in the presence of a catalyst nickel?
qs.e: This reaction involves the hydrogenation of ethene (C₂H₄), an unsaturated hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon double bond. In the presence of a nickel catalyst at moderate temperature, hydrogen (H₂) adds across the double bond, converting it to a single bond. The balanced chemical equation is: C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆. This yields ethane, a saturated hydrocarbon. Option 1 (propene) and Option 3 (propane) are incorrect because they contain three carbon atoms, whereas ethene has only two carbons—no carbon chain lengthening occurs. Option 2 (ethyne) is incorrect as it is an alkyne (C₂H₂) with a triple bond, not a hydrogenation product; hydrogenation would reduce ethyne to ethene or ethane, not form it from ethene.

qs.tag: RRB NTPC CBT-I : 1 April 2021 Shift 1
q: To neutralise the effect of formic acid injected by ant bite, which among the following can be used?
qs.e: Formic acid (HCOOH) is a weak organic acid injected by ants during bites. To neutralize an acid, a base is required. Among the options, sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) is a mild base commonly used as an antacid. It reacts with formic acid in a neutralization reaction to form sodium formate, water, and carbon dioxide: 2HCOOH + NaHCO₃ → HCOONa + H₂O + CO₂. This reaction is safe for skin application. Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) and potassium carbonate (K₂CO₃) are stronger bases that can cause skin irritation. Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is also a strong base (washing soda) and is too caustic for direct skin use. Sodium bicarbonate is preferred due to its mild nature and household availability.
qs.kf:
☛ Formic acid is also known as methanoic acid and is the simplest carboxylic acid. Sodium bicarbonate is commonly called baking soda and is used as an antacid and leavening agent. Neutralization reactions produce salt and water: Acid + Base → Salt + Water. Ant stings often contain formic acid, while bee stings contain methanoic acid (same as formic acid) and other compounds. Calcium carbonate is found in limestone, marble, and eggshells, and reacts with acids to produce CO₂ gas. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

qs.tag: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 : 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 2
q: Identify the simplest compound formed by carbon that is used widely as fuel.
qs.e: The simplest hydrocarbon compound formed by carbon that is widely used as fuel is methane (CH₄). Methane is the first member of the alkane series (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂) with only one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms. It occurs naturally as natural gas and is used extensively for heating, cooking, and electricity generation due to its high calorific value and clean combustion. Option 1 (methyl) is incorrect because it refers to the methyl group (-CH₃), which is a functional group, not a stable compound. Option 3 (ethane, C₂H₆) and option 4 (propane, C₃H₈) are also hydrocarbons but have two and three carbon atoms respectively, making them more complex than methane.

q: The IUPAC name for CH 3 COCH 3 is-

The parent alkane here is propane (C 3 H 8), so the IUPAC name becomes propanone. Acetone (Option 2) is the common name for this compound, not the IUPAC name. Propane (Option 3) is an alkane (C 3 H 8) without the carbonyl group, so it's incorrect. Dimethyl ketone (Option 4) is another common name describing the two methyl groups attached to the carbonyl carbon, but it's not the systematic IUPAC name.

q: Which of the following statements best describes allotropes of carbon?

qs.e: Allotropes are different structural modifications of the same element in the same physical state. Carbon exhibits several allotropes due to its ability to form strong covalent bonds in different arrangements. The most common allotropes are diamond (tetrahedral lattice), graphite (layered hexagonal structure), and fullerenes (spherical molecules like C 60). They have vastly different physical properties (e.g., diamond is hard and insulating, graphite is soft and conductive) but similar chemical properties as they all consist of pure carbon atoms and undergo similar reactions like combustion to form CO 2. Option 1 is incorrect because isotopes differ in neutron number, not structure. Option 2 is wrong as isomers apply to compounds, not elements. Option 3 is false as allotropes are pure elements, not compounds.

qs.tag: RRB JE CBT-I 2024 17 Dec 2024 Shift 2
q: Which of the following is NOT a homologous series?
o: C 3 H 7 OH, C 4 H 9 OH, C 5 H 11 OH, C 6 H 13 OH
CH 4, C 2 H 6, C 3 H 8, C 4 H 10
C 2 H 2, C 3 H 4, C 4 H 6, C 5 H 8
C 2 H 4, C 2 H 6, C 3 H 6, C 4 H 8
qs.e: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, and a general formula where successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit. Option 1 (C₃H₇OH to C₆H₁₃OH) represents alcohols with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, forming a homologous series. Option 3 (C₂H₂ to C₅H₈) represents alkynes with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, forming a homologous series. Option 4 (C₂H₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₆, C₄H₈) does NOT form a homologous series because it mixes different functional groups: C₂H₄ (ethene, alkene), C₂H₆ (ethane, alkane), C₃H₆ (propene, alkene), and C₄H₈ (butene, alkene). They lack a consistent functional group and the difference between successive members is not consistently –CH₂–.

☛ Isomerism is common in homologous series; for example, butane (C₄H₁₀) has two isomers: n-butane and isobutane.

q: What is the IUPAC name of adipic acid?

qs.tag: RRB Technician Grade III : 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 1
q: Heating of ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid yields which of the following?

q: ______ and water in the air react together to form carbonic acid.
qs.e: The correct answer is Carbon dioxide (CO₂) because it reacts with water (H₂O) in the atmosphere to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃). This is a reversible reaction: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃. Carbon monoxide (CO) does not form carbonic acid with water; it is a toxic gas that binds to hemoglobin. Elemental carbon (C) is insoluble in water and does not react directly to form carbonic acid. All of the options is incorrect because only carbon dioxide participates in this specific acid formation. This reaction is crucial in natural processes like ocean acidification and the carbon cycle.
qs.kf:
☛ Carbonic acid (H₂CO₃) is a weak, diprotic acid that partially dissociates in water. This reaction occurs naturally in rainwater, making it slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6). Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming. Carbon monoxide (CO) is produced by incomplete combustion and is poisonous. The equilibrium of CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ is important in blood buffering systems. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ CO₂ + H₂O forms which acid? → Carbonic acid (H₂CO₃)

qs.tag: RRB JE CBT I - : 2 June 2019 Shift 2
q: A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds that has-
o: Different number of carbon atoms and contain the different functional group
The same numbers of carbon atoms and contain the same functional group
Different number of carbon atoms but contain the same functional group
The same number of carbon atoms but contain same functional group
qs.e: A homologous series is defined as a family of organic compounds with the same functional group but a gradually increasing number of carbon atoms (typically differing by –CH₂– units). This results in compounds with similar chemical properties but gradually changing physical properties. Option 3 is correct because it accurately states "different number of carbon atoms but contain the same functional group." Option 1 is incorrect as different functional groups would create different series. Option 2 is wrong because same carbon atoms would mean identical compounds, not a series. Option 4 is incorrect as same carbon atoms with different functional groups represent isomers, not a homologous series.

☛ Homologous series members have similar chemical properties due to identical functional groups.
☛ Physical properties like melting point, boiling point increase with increasing molecular mass.
☛ Examples: Alkanes (methane, ethane, propane), Alkenes (ethene, propene, butene), Alcohols (methanol, ethanol, propanol).
☛ All members can be represented by a general molecular formula.
☛ Successive members differ by –CH₂– unit (methylene group) with molecular mass difference of 14 atomic mass units. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ How do physical properties change in a homologous series? → Boiling/melting points increase with molecular mass

qs.tag: RRB Technician Grade III : 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 3
q: Which statement is correct for unsaturated hydrocarbons?
o: Methane, ethane and butane are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Cyclo pentane and hexane are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Alkane, alkenes and alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Alkenes and alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
qs.e: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain double bonds (C=C) or triple bonds (C≡C) between carbon atoms, allowing them to undergo addition reactions. Alkenes (general formula C n H 2n) have at least one carbon-carbon double bond, while alkynes (C n H 2n-2) have at least one carbon-carbon triple bond. Option 1 is incorrect because methane (CH 4), ethane (C 2 H 6), and butane (C 4 H 10) are alkanes with only single bonds, making them saturated. Option 2 is wrong as cyclo pentane (C 5 H 10) and hexane (C 6 H 14) are saturated cyclic and straight-chain alkanes, respectively. Option 3 is incorrect because alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons, not unsaturated.

☛ Ethene (C 2 H 4) is the simplest alkene, used in polymer production like polyethylene.
☛ Ethyne (C 2 H 2), commonly called acetylene, is the simplest alkyne, used in welding torches.
☛ Saturated hydrocarbons undergo substitution reactions, while unsaturated ones undergo addition reactions.
☛ The IUPAC naming for alkenes uses the suffix "-ene" and for alkynes uses "- yne". Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ What is the general formula for alkenes? → C n H 2n

☛ Which hydrocarbon has a triple bond? → Alkyne
☛ What type of reaction do alkenes primarily undergo? → Addition reactions

q: Select the INCORRECT pair.

Pyruvate (pyruvic acid) is C₃H₄O₃ with 3 carbons. Ethanol is C₂H₅OH (C₂H₆O) with 2 carbons. Glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆ with 6 carbons. qs.tag: RPF Constable 2018 14 Feb 2019
q: Which of the following is used in making perfumes and aromatic substances?
qs.e: Esters are organic compounds formed by the reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, with the elimination of water. They are widely used in making perfumes and aromatic substances due to their pleasant, fruity odors. Esters like ethyl acetate (CH₃COOC₂H₅) and methyl butanoate (CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₃) are common in artificial flavorings and fragrances. Chlorine (Cl₂) is a toxic, pungent-smelling halogen gas used in disinfectants and bleaching agents, not in perfumes. Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is an alcohol used as a solvent and in alcoholic beverages, but it lacks the characteristic sweet smell of esters. Carbon (C) is a non-metallic element forming the basis of organic compounds but is not directly used in perfumery.
qs.kf:
☛ Esters are derivatives of carboxylic acids where the -OH group is replaced by an -OR' group.
☛ The reaction forming esters is called esterification, typically catalyzed by concentrated sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄).
☛ Natural esters are found in fruits (e.g., isoamyl acetate in bananas) and flowers, contributing to their aroma.
☛ Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of esters to form soap and alcohol.
☛ Esters are less polar than carboxylic acids, making them soluble in organic solvents but insoluble in water. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ Which compound gives fruits their characteristic smell? → Esters
☛ What is the product of esterification? → Ester and water
☛ Which catalyst is used in esterification? → Concentrated H₂SO₄
☛ What is the functional group of esters? → -COO-
☛ Which process converts esters to soap? → Saponification

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 11/12/2025 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM
q: Which of the following products is formed when carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide (lime water)?
qs.e: When carbon dioxide (CO₂) reacts with calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂), commonly known as lime water, it forms calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) and water. This is a neutralisation reaction where an acidic oxide (CO₂) reacts with a base (Ca(OH)₂). The balanced chemical equation is: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O. Calcium carbonate appears as a white precipitate, making lime water turn milky, which is a standard test for CO₂. Option 2 (calcium oxide, CaO) is incorrect because it is formed by thermal decomposition of CaCO₃, not from this reaction. Option 3 (sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃) is wrong as sodium is not involved. Option 4 (calcium bicarbonate, Ca(HCO₃)₂) forms when excess CO₂ reacts with CaCO₃ in water, not directly from Ca(OH)₂ under normal conditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is found naturally as limestone, marble, and chalk.
☛ The milky appearance in the lime water test is due to the formation of insoluble CaCO₃.
☛ Calcium bicarbonate (Ca(HCO₃)₂) is soluble in water and forms when excess CO₂ is passed through CaCO₃ suspension.
☛ Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂) is prepared by adding water to calcium oxide (CaO), a process called slaking.
☛ This reaction is used to remove CO₂ from gases in industrial processes and to test for CO₂ in breath. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What is the chemical formula of lime water? → Ca(OH)₂
☛ Which gas turns lime water milky? → Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
☛ What is the white precipitate formed when CO₂ is passed through lime water? → Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)
☛ What happens when excess CO₂ is passed through lime water? → Milky precipitate dissolves to form calcium bicarbonate (Ca(HCO₃)₂)
☛ What type of reaction is CO₂ with Ca(OH)₂? → Neutralisation reaction

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 22/12/2025 12:45 PM - 2:15 PM
q: Which compound from the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
qs.e: An unsaturated hydrocarbon contains at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) or triple bond (C≡C) in its structure. Ethene (C₂H₄) has a C=C double bond, making it unsaturated. In contrast, butane (C₄H₁₀), propane (C₃H₈), and methane (CH₄) are saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) with only single bonds (C-C) and follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Saturated hydrocarbons undergo substitution reactions (e.g., halogenation), while unsaturated hydrocarbons like ethene undergo addition reactions (e.g., with bromine water, which decolorizes). Thus, only ethene fits the definition of an unsaturated hydrocarbon.
qs.kf:
☛ Unsaturated hydrocarbons include alkenes (C=C) and alkynes (C≡C).
☛ Bromine water test is used to distinguish unsaturated hydrocarbons (decolorizes) from saturated ones (no change).
☛ Ethene is used in the production of polyethylene (plastic) via polymerization.
☛ Saturated hydrocarbons are less reactive than unsaturated ones due to the absence of multiple bonds.
☛ The simplest alkene is ethene, and the simplest alkyne is ethyne (C₂H₂). Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ Which hydrocarbon decolorizes bromine water? → Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes/alkynes)
☛ What is the general formula for alkenes? → CₙH₂ₙ
☛ Which compound has a carbon-carbon double bond? → Ethene (C₂H₄)
☛ What type of reaction do alkenes undergo? → Addition reactions
☛ Which is the simplest unsaturated hydrocarbon? → Ethene

qs.tag: RRB JE 25 May 2019 Shift 2 CBT 1
q: Which of the following is used as an antiseptic to sterilise wounds and syringes in hospitals?
qs.e: Ethyl alcohol (ethanol, C₂H₅OH) is commonly used as an antiseptic for sterilizing wounds and syringes in hospitals. This is because ethanol at concentrations of 70-80% effectively denatures proteins and disrupts the lipid membranes of microorganisms, leading to their death. Methanol (CH₃OH) is highly toxic and can cause blindness or death if ingested, making it unsuitable for medical use. Propanol (C₃H₇OH) and butanol (C₄H₉OH) are also alcohols but are less effective as antiseptics compared to ethanol; propanol is sometimes used in hand sanitizers but not typically for wound sterilization, while butanol has stronger solvent properties and is more irritating to skin. Ethanol's optimal bactericidal concentration (70-80%) provides better penetration than pure alcohol, making it the preferred choice in medical settings.
qs.kf:
☛ Ethanol is also known as grain alcohol and is produced by fermentation of sugars by yeast.
☛ Methanol is called wood alcohol and is highly poisonous; ingestion can cause metabolic acidosis.
☛ Isopropyl alcohol (C₃H₈O) is another common antiseptic used for disinfecting skin before injections.
☛ The antiseptic property of alcohols increases with molecular weight up to a point, but ethanol balances effectiveness and safety.
☛ Phenol (C₆H₅OH) was one of the first antiseptics used in surgery by Joseph Lister. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ Which alcohol is used as an antiseptic in hospitals? → Ethyl alcohol (ethanol)
☛ What is the common name of methanol? → Wood alcohol
☛ Which alcohol causes blindness upon ingestion? → Methanol
☛ What concentration of ethanol is most effective as an antiseptic? → 70-80%
☛ Which compound was the first surgical antiseptic? → Phenol

qs.tag: RRB JE CBT-I 2024 18 Dec 2024 Shift 3
q: An unsaturated carbohydrate that has a double bond is:
qs.e: An unsaturated hydrocarbon contains at least one double bond (C=C) or triple bond (C≡C) between carbon atoms. The general formula for alkenes (unsaturated hydrocarbons with one double bond) is C n H 2n. For C 3 H 6 (n=3), it satisfies this formula and represents propene (CH 3 -CH=CH 2), which has one double bond. C 3 H 4 (option 1) is propyne (triple bond, not double). C 3 H 8 (option 2) is propane (saturated alkane, no double bond). C 2 H 2 (option 3) is ethyne (triple bond, not double). Thus, only C 3 H 6 is an unsaturated hydrocarbon with a double bond.
qs.kf:
☛ Alkenes undergo addition reactions (e.g., with H 2, Br 2) due to the presence of double bonds.
☛ Propene (C 3 H 6) is used in the production of polypropylene, a common plastic.

☛ The IUPAC name for C 3 H 6 is propene, and its structural formula is CH 3 - CH=CH 2.

qs.tag: RPF SI 2018 : 11 Jan 2019 Shift 1
q: In cyclical structure of glucose, what is the cyclic organic composition made from the sum of an oxygen molecule and the sum of ﬁve carbon molecules?
qs.e: In the cyclic structure of glucose, the ring is formed by the combination of five carbon atoms and one oxygen atom, creating a six-membered heterocyclic ring called a pyranose ring. The term"pyren" (or pyran) specifically refers to this cyclic ether structure with the formula C 5 H 6 O, where five carbons and one oxygen form the ring. Glucose exists predominantly in this pyranose form in aqueous solution. Option 1 (Fructose) is incorrect because it's a different monosaccharide (ketohexose) that can form both pyranose and furanose rings. Option 3 (Anomam) is not a valid chemical term. Option 4 (Trio) refers to three-carbon compounds and is unrelated to glucose's cyclic structure.
qs.kf:
☛ Glucose exists in both open-chain and cyclic forms, with the cyclic form being more stable in solution.
☛ The cyclic structure forms through intramolecular reaction between the aldehyde group at C-1 and the hydroxyl group at C-5.
☛ Pyranose rings are six-membered (5C + 1O), while furanose rings are five-membered (4C + 1O).
☛ α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose are anomers that differ in configuration at the anomeric carbon (C-1).
☛ The systematic name for the pyranose form of glucose is D-glucopyranose. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What is the cyclic form of glucose with a six-membered ring called? → Pyranose form
☛ How many carbon atoms are in the pyranose ring of glucose? → Five carbon atoms
☛ Which atom besides carbon completes the glucose pyranose ring? → Oxygen atom
☛ What type of reaction forms the cyclic structure of glucose? → Intramolecular hemiacetal formation
☛ What are the two anomeric forms of D-glucose called? → α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose

q: If a carbon compound like propanol is oxidized in the presence of potassium dichromate, what is the most likely product formed?
qs.e: The oxidation of propanol (C₃H₇OH) with potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) in acidic medium is a standard organic reaction. Primary alcohols like propanol undergo oxidation first to aldehydes and then to carboxylic acids under strong oxidizing conditions. Since potassium dichromate is a strong oxidizing agent, it directly converts propanol to propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH). The balanced chemical equation is: 3CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + 2K₂Cr₂O₇ + 8H₂SO₄ → 3CH₃CH₂COOH + 2Cr₂(SO₄)₃ + 2K₂SO₄ + 11H₂O. Option 2 (methanol) is incorrect because oxidation doesn't reduce carbon chain length. Option 3 (propene) would form via dehydration, not oxidation. Option 4 (propane) is an alkane and results from reduction, not oxidation.
qs.kf:
☛ Potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) is a strong oxidizing agent used in organic chemistry for oxidation of alcohols.
☛ Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes and then to carboxylic acids; secondary alcohols oxidize to ketones; tertiary alcohols resist oxidation.
☛ Propanol (C₃H₇OH) exists as two isomers: propan-1-ol (primary) and propan-2-ol (secondary).
☛ The color change from orange (Cr₂O₇²⁻) to green (Cr³⁺) indicates completion of oxidation reaction.
☛ Propanoic acid (C₂H₅COOH) is a carboxylic acid with a pungent smell, used as preservative. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What does propanol oxidize to with K₂Cr₂O₇? → Propanoic acid
☛ Which alcohol gives carboxylic acid on oxidation? → Primary alcohol
☛ Color change when K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidizes alcohol? → Orange to green
☛ Oxidation product of ethanol with K₂Cr₂O₇? → Ethanoic acid (acetic acid)
☛ What is the formula of propanoic acid? → CH₃CH₂COOH

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 21/12/2025 12:45 PM - 2:15 PM
q: Which of the following carbon compounds shows the presence of a branched chain structure?
qs.e: In organic chemistry, alkanes can exist as straight-chain or branched-chain isomers. Butane (C₄H₁₀) has two structural isomers: n-butane (straight-chain) and iso-butane (branched-chain, also called 2-methylpropane). The question asks which compound shows the presenceof a branched structure, meaning it has at least one branched isomer. Methane (CH₄) and ethane (C₂H₆) have only one possible structure each (no isomers). Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) is a cyclic compound, not branched. Only butane among the options exhibits chain isomerism with a branched form, making option 3 correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Alkanes with formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ show chain isomerism when n ≥ 4.
☛ Iso-butane (2-methylpropane) has a branched structure with three carbon atoms in the main chain and one methyl group (-CH₃) attached.
☛ Cycloalkanes like cyclohexane have ring structures and formula CₙH₂ₙ, different from alkanes.
☛ Methane, ethane, propane (C₁ to C₃ alkanes) have no structural isomers.
☛ Branching affects physical properties: branched isomers generally have lower boiling points than straight-chain isomers. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ How many structural isomers does butane have? → Two (n-butane and iso-butane)
☛ Which compound has no structural isomers: methane, butane, or pentane? → Methane (CH₄)
☛ What is the general formula for alkanes? → CₙH₂ₙ₊₂

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 05/02/2026 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM
q: Which of the following is true about the homologous series?
o: All members have different functional groups.
All members have the same molecular weight.
Each successive member differs by -CH2- group.
All members have the same boiling point.
qs.e: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, where successive members differ by a -CH₂- unit (methylene group). This difference gives a constant increase in molecular weight of 14 atomic mass units. Option 1 is incorrect because all members have the same functional group (e.g., all alcohols have -OH). Option 2 is wrong as molecular weight increases regularly (e.g., methane CH₄ = 16, ethane C₂H₆ = 30). Option 4 is false because boiling points increase with molecular size due to stronger van der Waals forces (e.g., methanol boils at 65°C, ethanol at 78°C). Only option 3 correctly states the defining characteristic of homologous series.
qs.kf:
☛ Homologous series members show gradation in physical properties like boiling point, melting point, and density.
☛ All members of a homologous series can be represented by a general molecular formula (e.g., alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂).
☛ The chemical properties of homologous series members are similar due to identical functional groups.
☛ Examples include alkanes (paraffins), alkenes (olefins), alkynes (acetylenes), and alcohols.
☛ The first member of a homologous series often shows anomalous properties compared to higher members. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What is the difference between successive members of a homologous series? → -CH₂- group
☛ Do members of a homologous series have the same functional group? → Yes
☛ What happens to boiling point in a homologous series as molecular weight increases? → Increases

☛ Which series has general formula CₙH₂ₙ? → Alkenes

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 23/12/2025 12:45 PM - 2:15 PM
q: Which of the following represents a straight chain hydrocarbon?
qs.e: A straight chain hydrocarbon (also called normal or n-alkane) has all carbon atoms arranged in a continuous, unbranched chain without any rings. Butane (C₄H₁₀) has the structure CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃, which is a straight chain. Cyclopentane (C₅H₁₀) is a cyclic hydrocarbon with a ring structure. Isobutane (C₄H₁₀) is a branched isomer of butane with structure (CH₃)₃CH. Benzene (C₆H₆) is an aromatic hydrocarbon with a hexagonal ring structure. Only butane among the options has no branches or rings, making it the correct straight chain hydrocarbon.

qs.tag: RRB JE CBT I - : 31 May 2019 Shift 1
q: A cyclic hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C 6 H 6 is -
qs.e: The molecular formula C 6 H 6 corresponds to benzene, which is a cyclic hydrocarbon with a hexagonal ring structure. Benzene is an aromatic hydrocarbon with alternating single and double bonds (resonance hybrid). Methane (CH 4) is not cyclic. Naphthalene has formula C 10 H 8 and contains two fused benzene rings. q: Atomic masses of elements are compared with a standard reference. Carbon-12 was chosen as the standard for the atomic mass unit mainly because:
o: Carbon is present in very large amounts in nature
Carbon shows very little chemical reactivity with elements
Carbon-12 gives atomic masses close to whole numbers
Carbon is able to form a large number of compounds
qs.e: The atomic mass unit (amu) is defined as 1/12th the mass of one atom of carbon-12. Carbon-12 was chosen as the standard reference because its atomic mass is exactly 12 amu by definition, making the atomic masses of other elements close to whole numbers when measured relative to it. This simplifies calculations and comparisons in chemistry. Option 1 is incorrect because abundance (e.g., oxygen or hydrogen are also abundant) was not the primary criterion. Option 2 is wrong as carbon is chemically reactive, forming numerous compounds. Option 4 is incorrect since the ability to form compounds (catenation) is unrelated to the atomic mass standardisation.
qs.kf:
☛ Before 1961, oxygen-16 was used as the atomic mass standard (1 amu = 1/16 mass of oxygen-16).
☛ The unified atomic mass unit (u) or dalton (Da) is now the accepted SI unit for atomic masses.
☛ Carbon-12 has 6 protons and 6 neutrons, making it stable and ideal for mass spectrometry measurements.
☛ Relative atomic mass is a dimensionless ratio comparing an element's average atomic mass to 1/12th of carbon-12's mass.
☛ Hydrogen-1 has an atomic mass of approximately 1.008 amu, slightly more than 1 due to isotopic abundance and binding energy. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What is the standard for atomic mass unit? → Carbon-12
☛ 1 amu is equal to? → 1/12th mass of one carbon-12 atom
☛ Why was carbon-12 chosen over oxygen-16? → To get atomic masses closer to whole numbers
☛ What is the atomic mass of carbon-12 in amu? → Exactly 12.0000 amu
☛ Which isotope is used in mass spectrometry calibration? → Carbon-12

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 06/02/2026 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM
q: Which of the following is a straight-chain saturated hydrocarbon?
qs.e: A straight-chain saturated hydrocarbon is an alkane with only single bonds between carbon atoms and no branching or cyclic structure. Butane (C₄H₁₀) has the molecular formula C₄H₁₀ and a linear structure: CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃, with all carbon-carbon bonds as single bonds, making it saturated and straight-chain. Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) is cyclic, not straight-chain. Propene (C₃H₆) contains a carbon-carbon double bond, making it unsaturated (an alkene). Benzene (C₆H₆) is an aromatic hydrocarbon with a cyclic structure and delocalized π-electrons, not saturated or straight-chain. Thus, only butane fits both criteria.
qs.kf:
☛ Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

q: In which carbon allotrope are atoms arranged in a hexagonal layer structure, with weak forces between layers?
qs.e: Graphite is the carbon allotrope where atoms are arranged in hexagonal layers with weak van der Waals forces between layers. Each carbon atom in graphite is sp² hybridized and forms three strong covalent bonds with neighboring atoms within the same layer, creating a planar hexagonal network. The fourth electron of each carbon atom is delocalized, making graphite a good conductor of electricity. The layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide over each other, giving graphite its lubricating property. Diamond has a tetrahedral 3D network with strong covalent bonds in all directions. Coke is an amorphous form of carbon produced by heating coal in absence of air. Fullerenes are spherical or tubular molecules like C₆₀ (buckminsterfullerene).

q: Which of the following form a set of homologous series?
qs.e: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, where successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit. Option 2 contains ethyne (C₂H₂), propyne (C₃H₄), and butyne (C₄H₆), all alkynes with the –C≡C– triple bond functional group. They follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ and differ by –CH₂– increments. Option 1 mixes alkanes (ethane, methane) with an alkyne (ethyne), having different functional groups. Option 3 mixes alkynes (ethyne, propyne) with an alkene (butene), violating the same functional group rule. Option 4 mixes alkanes (ethane, methane) with an alkene (propene), again lacking a common functional group.

q: Which of the following is a ring-chain hydrocarbon?
qs.e: A ring-chain hydrocarbon (also called cyclic hydrocarbon) is an organic compound where carbon atoms are arranged in a closed ring structure. Ethene (C₂H₄) is an alkene with a straight-chain structure containing a carbon-carbon double bond. Propane (C₃H₈) is an alkane with a simple straight-chain structure of three carbon atoms. Heptyne (C₇H₁₂) is an alkyne with a straight-chain structure containing a carbon-carbon triple bond. Only benzene has the characteristic ring structure required for a ring-chain hydrocarbon.

q: Which branch of chemistry deals with the study of elements and compounds that do not contain carbon-hydrogen bonds?
qs.e: The question asks about the branch of chemistry that studies elements and compounds lacking carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds. Inorganic chemistry specifically deals with all chemical compounds except those containing C-H bonds, which are the domain of organic chemistry. This includes metals, minerals, salts, acids, bases, and coordination compounds. Organic chemistry (Option 1) focuses on carbon-containing compounds, especially hydrocarbons and derivatives with C-H bonds. Biochemistry (Option 2) studies chemical processes in living organisms, which primarily involve organic compounds. Physical chemistry (Option 3) applies physics principles to chemical systems, regardless of bond types. Thus, only inorganic chemistry excludes C-H bonded compounds by definition.

q: Which of the following allotropes of carbon conducts electricity?
qs.e: Graphite is the only allotrope of carbon among the given options that conducts electricity. This property arises from its unique layered structure where each carbon atom is sp² hybridized and forms three covalent bonds in a hexagonal planar arrangement, leaving one delocalized electron per carbon atom that can move freely between layers. These mobile electrons allow graphite to conduct electricity. Diamond does not conduct electricity because all four valence electrons of each carbon atom are involved in sp³ hybridized tetrahedral covalent bonds, leaving no free electrons. Charcoal is an amorphous form of carbon with disordered structure that lacks continuous electron pathways. Fullerene molecules (like C₆₀) have localized π-electrons within each molecule but poor inter-molecular electron transfer, making them insulators or semiconductors, not good conductors like graphite.

q: What is the molecular formula of butane?
qs.e: Butane is a saturated hydrocarbon belonging to the alkane series. The general formula for alkanes is C n H 2n+2. For butane, the prefix "but-" indicates 4 carbon atoms (n=4). Substituting n=4 into the formula gives: C 4 H (2×4+2) = C 4 H 10. This is why option 4 is correct. Option 1 (C 5 H 12) is pentane, option 2 (C 2 H 6) is ethane, and option 3 (C 3 H 8) is propane —all are alkanes but with different carbon chain lengths. Butane exists in two structural isomers: n-butane (straight chain) and isobutane (branched chain), both having the same molecular formula C 4 H 10.

q: Which alcohol is commonly used as fuel?
qs.e: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is the most commonly used alcohol as fuel, particularly in the form of gasohol (blended with gasoline) or as a biofuel. This is because ethanol has a high octane rating (around 113), burns cleanly with lower emissions compared to fossil fuels, and can be produced renewably from biomass fermentation. While methanol (CH₃OH) is also used as fuel in some racing applications and fuel cells, it is more toxic and corrosive. Propanol (C₃H₇OH) and butanol (C₄H₉OH) have higher energy content but are less commonly used due to production costs and engine compatibility issues. Ethanol's widespread adoption stems from its balance of performance, renewable production via fermentation of sugars, and established infrastructure for blending with petroleum fuels.

q: A cyclic compound that contains only single bonds is classified as:
qs.e: In organic chemistry, saturated compounds contain only single bonds (C–C and C–H) with no double or triple bonds. A cyclic compound with only single bonds is specifically called a cycloalkane (e.g., cyclohexane, C₆H₁₂), which is saturated. Aliphatic compounds (option 1) can be cyclic or acyclic but include both saturated and unsaturated types. Aromatic compounds (option 2) are cyclic with alternating double and single bonds (e.g., benzene, C₆H₆), making them unsaturated. Unsaturated compounds (option 4) contain at least one double or triple bond. Thus, only option 3 correctly describes a cyclic compound with only single bonds.

q: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
qs.e: Saturated hydrocarbons are compounds containing only single bonds between carbon atoms, with the general formula C n H 2n+2. Methane (CH 4) has only single C-H bonds and fits this formula (n=1, H=4). Propylene (C 3 H 6) contains a carbon-carbon double bond, making it an unsaturated alkene. Butadiene (C 4 H 6) has two double bonds, classifying it as a diene. Acetylene (C 2 H 2) contains a triple bond, making it an alkyne. Only methane has all single bonds and maximum hydrogen atoms per carbon, satisfying the definition of a saturated hydrocarbon.

q: Which of the following is the correct formula for ethyne?
qs.e: Ethyne (common name: acetylene) is the simplest alkyne with a triple bond between two carbon atoms. The general formula for alkynes is C n H 2n-2. For ethyne, n=2, so the formula becomes C 2 H 2. This represents two carbon atoms connected by a triple bond (C≡C) and each carbon bonded to one hydrogen atom. Option 1 (CH 4) is methane (alkane). Option 3 (C 2 H 4) is ethene (alkene with double bond). Option 4 (C 2 H 6) is ethane (alkane with single bond). Only C 2 H 2 correctly represents ethyne's triple bond structure.

q: Which of the following alcohols is used in cough syrups?
qs.e: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is the alcohol commonly used in cough syrups and medicinal preparations. This is because ethanol acts as an effective solvent for many active pharmaceutical ingredients, helps preserve the formulation by inhibiting microbial growth, and serves as a cough suppressant in appropriate concentrations. Methanol (CH₃OH) is highly toxic and causes blindness or death if ingested, making it unsuitable for medicinal use. Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) is vinegar's main component and an acid, not an alcohol, so it doesn't belong in this category. Propanol (C₃H₇OH) has industrial applications but is more irritating and less safe than ethanol for internal use. Pharmaceutical-grade ethanol is specially denatured to prevent misuse while maintaining therapeutic efficacy.

☛ Methanol is called "wood alcohol" and is extremely poisonous—even 10 mL can cause permanent blindness.

qs.tag: RRB Technician Grade III 06/03/2026 12:45 PM - 2:15 PM
q: If the molecular mass of an alkane is 44, then its molecular formula is:
qs.e: The general formula for alkanes is C n H 2n+2. To find the molecular formula with molecular mass 44, we calculate: Atomic mass of C = 12, H = 1. For C n H 2n+2, molecular mass = 12n + 1(2n+2) = 12n + 2n + 2 = 14n + 2. Set 14n + 2 = 44 → 14n = 42 → n = 3. Thus, formula is C₃H₈ (propane). Why correct: C₃H₈ has mass = (3×12) + (8×1) = 36 + 8 = 44. Why wrong: C₂H₆ mass = 30, C₄H₁₀ mass = 58, CH₄ mass = 16 — none match 44.
qs.kf:
☛ Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds (C–C, C–H).
☛ The simplest alkane is methane (CH₄), a major component of natural gas.

q: Which of the following is a homologous series?
qs.e: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, and successive members differing by a –CH₂– unit. Methane (CH₄), Ethane (C₂H₆), and Propane (C₃H₈) are all alkanes with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. They differ by –CH₂– units: CH₄ → C₂H₆ (+CH₂) → C₃H₈ (+CH₂). Option 1 (Ethene, Ethyne, Ethane) includes different hydrocarbon classes (alkene, alkyne, alkane). Option 2 (Methane, Ethane, Ethene) mixes alkanes and an alkene. Option 4 (Methane, Methanol, Methanoic acid) contains different functional groups (alkane, alcohol, carboxylic acid). Only Option 3 satisfies all criteria of a homologous series.
qs.kf:
☛ Homologous series members show a gradual change in physical properties (e.g., boiling point increases with molecular mass).
☛ All members of a homologous series can be prepared by similar methods and undergo similar chemical reactions.
☛ The difference in molecular formula between successive members is CH₂ (molar mass difference = 14 g/mol).
☛ Other important homologous series include alkenes (CₙH₂ₙ), alkynes (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂), and alcohols (CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH).

☛ What is the molecular formula of Propane? → C₃H₈

qs.tag: RRB JE CBT-I : 22 May, 2019 Shift 2
q: Functional group -CHO is present in which of the following?
qs.e: The functional group -CHO (aldehyde group) consists of a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to a hydrogen atom and an R group (alkyl/aryl). This structure is characteristic of aldehydes, with the general formula R-CHO. In ketones (Option 1), the carbonyl group is bonded to two carbon atoms (R-CO-R'), not hydrogen. Alcohols (Option 3) contain the -OH (hydroxyl) group. Carboxylic acids (Option 4) have the -COOH group, which includes -OH bonded to the carbonyl carbon. The aldehyde group is easily identified by its terminal position in carbon chains and its reactivity in oxidation reactions to form carboxylic acids.

qs.tag: RRB JE 27 May 2019 Shift 2 CBT 1
q: Which of the following is the first member of alkyne homologous series?
qs.e: The alkyne homologous series consists of unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C). According to IUPAC nomenclature, the first member must have the smallest possible carbon chain with this functional group. Ethyne (C₂H₂) has two carbon atoms with one triple bond, making it the simplest alkyne. Ethene (C₂H₄) is an alkene with a double bond, not an alkyne. Propyne (C₃H₄) has three carbons and is a higher homologue. Methane (CH₄) is an alkane with only single bonds. Thus, only ethyne satisfies the criteria of being the first member with molecular formula C n H 2n-2 where n=2.

q: When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulfuric acid at 170 °C, what is the main product?
qs.e: When ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is heated with excess concentrated sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) at 170°C, it undergoes dehydration (removal of water molecule) to form ethene (C₂H₄). This is an elimination reaction where sulfuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent and catalyst. The balanced chemical equation is: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O. Option 1 (ethanoic acid) is incorrect because ethanol oxidation to ethanoic acid requires oxidizing agents like acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, not dehydration. Option 3 (methanol) is wrong as it's a different alcohol with one carbon atom. Option 4 (propanol) is incorrect since it has three carbons and isn't formed from ethanol dehydration.
qs.kf:
☛ Ethene (C₂H₄) is the simplest alkene with a double bond between carbon atoms.
☛ At lower temperatures (140°C), ethanol with concentrated H₂SO₄ produces diethyl ether (C₂H₅OC₂H₅) via intermolecular dehydration.
☛ Concentrated sulfuric acid is hygroscopic and commonly used as a dehydrating agent in laboratories.
☛ Ethanol can also be dehydrated using alumina (Al₂O₃) as catalyst at 350°C.
☛ The dehydration reaction follows Saytzeff's rule for alkene formation from alcohols. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What is formed when ethanol is heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 140°C? → Diethyl ether
☛ Which catalyst is used for dehydration of ethanol to ethene? → Concentrated sulfuric acid
☛ What type of reaction is ethanol → ethene? → Dehydration/elimination reaction
☛ What is the IUPAC name of C₂H₄? → Ethene
☛ Which gas is produced when ethanol is dehydrated? → Ethene gas

qs.tag: RRB JE 25 May 2019 Shift 3 CBT 1
q: Cooking gas (LPG) mainly consists of-
qs.e: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), commonly known as cooking gas, is a mixture of hydrocarbon gases. It primarily consists of propane (C₃H₈) and butane (C₄H₁₀), which are alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons). These gases are compressed into liquid form for storage and transport in cylinders. When released, they vaporize and burn efficiently with a clean blue flame, making them ideal for domestic cooking. Option 1 (ethene) and option 2 (ethyne) are unsaturated hydrocarbons used in industrial processes like polymerization and welding, not in LPG. Option 3 (propene) is an alkene used in plastics production. Thus, only option 4 correctly identifies the main components of LPG.
qs.kf:

☛ Propane has a lower boiling point (-42°C) than butane (-0.5°C), making it suitable for colder climates.
☛ Combustion of propane: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O + heat (balanced equation).
☛ LPG is heavier than air; leaks can accumulate at ground level, posing explosion risks.
☛ It is a fossil fuel derived from petroleum refining or natural gas processing. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

q: A molecule of methane contains one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms. What is the chemical formula for methane?
qs.e: The chemical formula for methane is CH₄. Methane is the simplest alkane and the first member of the homologous series of alkanes. It consists of one carbon atom (C) bonded to four hydrogen atoms (H) through single covalent bonds, forming a tetrahedral geometry. Carbon has a valency of 4 and hydrogen has a valency of 1, so one carbon atom combines with four hydrogen atoms to satisfy the octet rule, resulting in the formula CH₄. Option 2 (CH₃) is incorrect because it represents a methyl group, not a complete molecule. Option 3 (C₄H) is incorrect as it doesn't follow carbon's tetravalency. Option 4 (C₂H₄) is incorrect because it represents ethene, an alkene with a double bond between carbon atoms.
qs.kf:
☛ Methane is the main component of natural gas and biogas.
☛ Methane is a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential about 25 times that of CO₂ over 100 years.
☛ Methane undergoes combustion to produce carbon dioxide and water: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
☛ Methane is produced naturally by methanogenic archaea in anaerobic environments.
☛ The IUPAC name for methane is methane, and it follows the general formula for alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

q: Which of the following belongs to the alkyne group?
qs.e: The alkyne group consists of hydrocarbons with at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C). The general formula for alkynes is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. Among the options: C₃H₈ (propane) is an alkane with formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; C₆H₆ (benzene) is an aromatic compound with formula CₙHₙ; C₂H₄ (ethene) is an alkene with formula CₙH₂ₙ. Only C₃H₄ fits the alkyne formula: for n=3, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ gives C₃H₄, which is propyne (CH₃-C≡CH). Alkynes undergo addition reactions like hydrogenation to form alkenes/alkanes, and hydration to form carbonyl compounds. Their triple bond makes them more reactive than alkanes/alkenes in many reactions.

q: Ethanoic acid reacts with alcohols to form what compound?
qs.e: Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) reacts with alcohols (R-OH) in the presence of an acid catalyst (like concentrated H₂SO₄) to form esters through a esterification reaction. The balanced chemical equation is: CH₃COOH + R-OH → CH₃COOR + H₂O. This is a condensation reaction where water is eliminated. Option 1 (Esters) is correct because esterification specifically produces esters. Option 2 (Alcohols) is incorrect as alcohols are reactants, not products. Option 3 (Ketone) is wrong because ketones are typically formed from secondary alcohol oxidation, not acid-alcohol reactions. Option 4 (Aldehyde) is incorrect as aldehydes form from primary alcohol oxidation.

q: When methane (CH 4) burns completely in the presence of sufficient oxygen, which products are formed?
qs.e: The complete combustion of methane (CH₄) in sufficient oxygen produces carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O). This is an exothermic oxidation reaction where methane reacts with oxygen to form these products. The balanced chemical equation is: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. In complete combustion, all carbon atoms are oxidized to CO₂, and all hydrogen atoms form H₂O. Option 1 is incorrect because carbon (C) is not a product of complete combustion; it forms only in incomplete combustion. Option 2 is wrong as hydrogen (H₂) is not released; it combines with oxygen to form water. Option 4 is incorrect because carbon monoxide (CO) is produced only in incomplete combustion due to insufficient oxygen.

q: Intestinal juice converts protein in food into which molecules?
qs.e: The digestion of proteins involves their breakdown into simpler units. Intestinal juice contains enzymes like trypsin, chymotrypsin, and peptidases that hydrolyze proteins. Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. During digestion, these peptide bonds are broken through hydrolysis, converting proteins into their constituent amino acids. Option 2 is correct because amino acids are the final products of protein digestion in the small intestine. Option 1 (glycerol) and Option 3 (fatty acids) are products of lipid digestion, not protein. Option 4 (glucose) is a product of carbohydrate digestion. Thus, only amino acids result from protein breakdown by intestinal enzymes.

q: What is the common name of chloroethene?

q: The process of fermentation involves the conversion of sugars into which of the following compounds?
qs.e: The process of fermentation involves the anaerobic conversion of sugars (like glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆) into ethanol (C₂H₅OH) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) by the action of yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). This is a biochemical oxidation-reduction process where glucose is broken down without oxygen. The correct answer is ethanol (Option 4) because it is the primary alcohol produced. Ethene (Option 1) is an alkene obtained by dehydration of ethanol, not directly from fermentation. Methane (Option 2) is produced by anaerobic digestion of organic matter, not sugar fermentation. Ethanoic acid (Option 3) is formed by oxidation of ethanol, typically via acetic acid bacteria.

qs.tag: RRB JE CE 22 Apr 2025 Shift 2 CBT 2
q: Identify the correct formula for the compound formed between Mg 2+ and PO 4 3- ions.
qs.e: In ionic compounds, the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge for electrical neutrality. Mg 2+ has a +2 charge, and PO 4 3- has a -3 charge. The lowest common multiple of 2 and 3 is 6. To achieve a total charge of +6, we need 3 Mg 2+ ions (3 × +2 = +6). To achieve a total charge of -6, we need 2 PO 4 3- ions (2 × -3 = -6). Thus, the formula is Mg 3 (PO 4) 2. Option 1 (MgPO 4) is incorrect because charges don't balance (+2 vs -3). Option 2 (Mg 3 (PO 4) 3) gives +6 and -9 charges. Option 4 (Mg(PO 4) 3) gives +2 and -9 charges.
qs.kf:
☛ Magnesium phosphate (Mg 3 (PO 4) 2) is a white crystalline solid insoluble in water.
☛ The phosphate ion (PO 4 3-) is a polyatomic ion with tetrahedral geometry.
☛ Magnesium is an alkaline earth metal (Group 2) that always forms +2 ions in compounds.

q: Which law states that a compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass?
qs.e: The Law of Definite Proportions (also called Proust's Law) states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed and definite proportions by mass, regardless of its source or method of preparation. For example, pure water (H₂O) always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a mass ratio of 1:8 (or 11.11% hydrogen and 88.89% oxygen by mass). This law applies to all pure compounds. Option 1 (Law of Conservation of Mass) states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions. Option 3 (Law of Multiple Proportions) applies when two elements form more than one compound, with masses of one element combining with a fixed mass of the other in ratios of small whole numbers. Option 4 (Avogadro's Law) relates volume and number of moles of gases at constant temperature and pressure.

☛ This law applies only to pure chemical compounds, not to mixtures or solutions.

☛ The law helped establish Dalton's Atomic Theory which explains it through fixed atomic combinations. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ What is the mass ratio of hydrogen to oxygen in water? → 1:8

CO₂ + NaOH → NaHCO₃ (with limited CO₂) 2. 2NaOH + CO₂ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O (with excess CO₂) CO₂ is correct because it's an acidic oxide that reacts with bases like NaOH to form carbonate/bicarbonate salts. q: How are ionic compounds formed between metals and non-metals?
o: By transfer of electrons from metal atoms to non-metal atoms.
By sharing of electrons between atoms.
By the formation of a sea of delocalised electrons.
By mutual attraction between positively charged nuclei
qs.e: Ionic compounds are formed through ionic bonding, which occurs between metals and non-metals. Metals have low ionization energies and tend to lose electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, forming positively charged cations (e.g., Na⁺ from sodium). Non-metals have high electron affinities and tend to gain electrons to achieve stability, forming negatively charged anions (e.g., Cl⁻ from chlorine). The transfer of electrons from metal atoms to non-metal atoms creates these ions, which are then held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction (Coulombic forces). For example, in sodium chloride (NaCl), sodium transfers one electron to chlorine: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻ and Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻. Option 2 describes covalent bonding (e.g., in H₂O), option 3 describes metallic bonding (e.g., in copper), and option 4 is incomplete— attraction between nuclei alone does not form compounds without electron involvement.

☛ Common examples include NaCl (table salt), MgO (magnesium oxide), and CaCl₂ (calcium chloride).
☛ The lattice energy released during formation determines the stability of ionic compounds. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ Which property is high in ionic compounds? → Melting and boiling points
☛ What is formed when a metal loses an electron? → Cation (positive ion)
☛ Give an example of an ionic compound soluble in water. → Sodium chloride (NaCl)

q: Which type of bond is present between carbon atoms in saturated hydrocarbons?
qs.e: In saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), all carbon atoms are bonded to the maximum number of hydrogen atoms possible, meaning they contain only single bonds (C–C and C–H). This is because saturated hydrocarbons have the general formula C n H 2n+2 and follow the tetravalency of carbon with sp 3 hybridization. Each carbon forms four single covalent bonds, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry. Option 1 (both double and triple bonds) is incorrect because saturated hydrocarbons contain no multiple bonds. Option 3 (double bond) and Option 4 (triple bond) are characteristic of unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes respectively), which have fewer hydrogen atoms.

q: Which statement best defines the term 'formula unit mass' as used in the context of ionic compounds?

It is the mass of one mole of a molecular compound.

qs.e: Formula unit mass is specifically defined for ionic compounds, which do not exist as discrete molecules but as three-dimensional crystal lattices. A formula unit represents the simplest ratio of ions in the compound (e.g., NaCl for sodium chloride). The formula unit mass is calculated by summing the atomic masses (from the periodic table) of all atoms in one formula unit. For example, for NaCl : Atomic mass of Na = 23 u, Cl = 35.5 u → Formula unit mass = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 u. Option 1 is incorrect because it refers to the atom count in covalent molecules, not ionic compounds. Option 2 describes molar mass (mass of one mole), which is related but not the same as formula unit mass (which is in atomic mass units). Option 3 is wrong as it mentions the product of atomic masses, which is not used in mass calculations.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE for all saturated hydrocarbons?

qs.e: Saturated hydrocarbons, also known as alkanes, contain only single covalent bonds (C–C and C–H) and have the general formula C n H 2n+2. Due to the presence of strong sigma bonds and low polarity, they are relatively unreactive under normal conditions. They do not contain double or triple bonds, so they cannot undergo addition reactions, which require unsaturated bonds. Instead, under appropriate conditions (like UV light or heat with halogens), they undergo substitution reactions where hydrogen atoms are replaced by other atoms or groups. Option 1 is incorrect because triple bonds are characteristic of alkynes, not saturated hydrocarbons. Option 2 is wrong as addition reactions are typical of alkenes and alkynes. Option 3 is false because saturated hydrocarbons have only single bonds.

q: In which of the following phenomena is solid state directly transformed into gaseous state without changing into liquid state?
qs.e: The direct transition of a substance from the solid state to the gaseous state without passing through the liquid state is called sublimation. This occurs when the vapor pressure of the solid exceeds the atmospheric pressure at a temperature below its melting point. Common examples include dry ice (solid CO₂) sublimating to carbon dioxide gas and iodine crystals forming violet vapors. Fusion (melting) is solid to liquid, deposition is gas to solid (reverse of sublimation), and solidification (freezing) is liquid to solid. Thus, only sublimation matches the described phenomenon.

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 11/12/2025 12:45 PM - 2:15 PM
q: Which of the following is NOT formed in the chlor-alkali process?
qs.e: The chlor-alkali process involves the electrolysis of a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride (NaCl) using a diaphragm or membrane cell. During electrolysis, chlorine gas (Cl₂) is produced at the anode through oxidation: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. At the cathode, hydrogen gas (H₂) is formed by reduction of water: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻. The remaining sodium ions (Na⁺) combine with hydroxide ions (OH⁻) to produce sodium hydroxide (NaOH). Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is NOT formed in this process; it is typically produced via the Solvay process using ammonia, carbon dioxide, and sodium chloride. Thus, option 4 is correct because sodium carbonate is absent, while chlorine gas, sodium hydroxide, and hydrogen gas are all primary products.
qs.kf:

q: Unsaturated carbons are _______ than the saturated carbon compounds.
qs.e: Unsaturated carbon compounds contain double or triple bonds (π-bonds) between carbon atoms, while saturated compounds have only single bonds (σ-bonds). The π-bonds in unsaturated hydrocarbons are weaker and more accessible to electrophiles/nucleophiles due to higher electron density, making them more reactive. Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) have strong C–C and C–H σ-bonds, requiring harsh conditions for reactions. Option 1 is incorrect because unsaturated means less saturated. Option 3 is wrong as reactivity differs significantly. Option 4 is false because unsaturated compounds undergo addition reactions readily, unlike saturated ones.

q: Which among the following organic compounds is saturated?

Bromopropane (C₃H₇Br) has the structure CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–Br with only single bonds, making it saturated. q: What is the molecular formula of washing soda?

q: When litmus is added to a solution of borax, it turns ___________.
qs.e: When litmus is added to a borax solution, it turns blue because borax (sodium tetraborate decahydrate, Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O) produces an alkaline solution in water. Borax undergoes hydrolysis in water to form sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and boric acid (H₃BO₃). The reaction is: Na₂B₄O₇ + 7H₂O → 2NaOH + 4H₃BO₃. The NaOH makes the solution basic, with a pH > 7. Litmus is a natural pH indicator that turns red in acidic conditions (pH < 7) and blue in basic conditions (pH > 7). Since borax solution is basic, litmus turns blue. Options 1, 2, and 3 (pink, orange, red) are incorrect because they indicate acidic or neutral conditions, which do not occur here.

qs.tag: RRB JE CBT I - : 2 June 2019 Shift 1
q: What is the colour of sunlight when scattered by the air molecules in the atmosphere?
qs.e: This phenomenon is explained by Rayleigh scattering, which states that scattering intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ∝ 1/λ⁴). Blue light has a shorter wavelength (≈450-495 nm) compared to red light (≈620-750 nm), so it scatters about 10 times more effectively in the atmosphere. During daytime, this scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions, making the sky appear blue. White is incorrect because sunlight appears white only before scattering. Red is incorrect as red scatters least and dominates during sunrise/sunset when light travels longer through atmosphere. VIBGYOR (visible spectrum) is incorrect because it represents all colors before scattering, not the scattered result.
qs.kf:
☛ Rayleigh scattering explains why the sky is blue and sunsets appear red
☛ The scattering effect is more pronounced for smaller particles (like air molecules) compared to larger particles
☛ This phenomenon is named after British physicist Lord Rayleigh (John William Strutt)
☛ In the absence of atmosphere (like on the Moon), the sky appears black because there's no scattering
☛ The violet light scatters even more than blue, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, so we perceive the sky as blue Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ Why is the sky blue during daytime? → Due to Rayleigh scattering of shorter wavelength blue light by air molecules
☛ What law explains the blue color of the sky? → Rayleigh scattering law (I ∝ 1/λ⁴)
☛ Which color scatters most in the atmosphere? → Violet scatters most, but blue is perceived due to eye sensitivity
☛ Why do sunsets appear red? → During sunset, light travels longer path through atmosphere, scattering blue away, leaving red
☛ What would be the sky color without atmosphere? → Black (as on the Moon)

q: By which unit do the successive members of the homogenous series CH 4, C 2 H 6, and C 3 H 8 differ from each other?
qs.e: The compounds CH 4 (methane), C 2 H 6 (ethane), and C 3 H 8 (propane) form a homologous series of alkanes. In a homologous series, successive members differ by a −CH 2 − unit (methylene group). This is verified by comparing molecular formulas: C 2 H 6 minus CH 4 equals CH 2, and C 3 H 8 minus C 2 H 6 also equals CH 2. Option 2 (CH 4) is incorrect because it represents the first member itself, not the difference. Option 3 (CH) is wrong as it doesn't match the actual difference in composition. Option 4 (CH 3) is incorrect because alkanes differ by CH 2, not CH 3; CH 3 would imply a difference of one carbon and three hydrogens, which doesn't balance the hydrogen count between successive members.

☛ Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds (C−C and C−H).
☛ The −CH 2 − unit adds approximately 14 atomic mass units to each successive member.
☛ Other homologous series include alkenes (C n H 2n) and alkynes (C n H 2n-2), each with their own difference unit.

q: In a micelle, which part faces outward toward water?
qs.e: In micelles, which are spherical aggregates formed by amphiphilic molecules like soaps or detergents in aqueous solutions, the ionic (hydrophilic) head faces outward toward water. This occurs because the hydrophilic (water-loving) ionic head contains polar or charged groups (e.g., carboxylate -COO⁻ in soaps) that interact favorably with water molecules through hydrogen bonding and ion-dipole interactions. Conversely, the hydrophobic (water-fearing) hydrocarbon tails face inward, away from water, minimizing contact with it. Option 1 (Hydrocarbon tail) is incorrect as it faces inward. Option 3 (Non-polar end) is essentially the same as the hydrocarbon tail and faces inward. Option 4 (Grease molecule) is incorrect because grease is trapped inside the micelle, not facing outward.
qs.kf:
☛ Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids (e.g., sodium stearate C₁₇H₃₅COONa).
☛ Detergents are synthetic amphiphiles like sodium lauryl sulfate (C₁₂H₂₅OSO₃⁻Na⁺).
☛ Micelles help in emulsification of oils and grease by trapping non-polar substances inside.
☛ The process of cleaning with soaps involves micelle formation where dirt/grease is encapsulated.
☛ Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC) decreases with increase in hydrophobic chain length. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

☛ What is the minimum concentration for micelle formation called? → Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC).
☛ Why do hydrocarbon tails face inward in micelles? → To avoid water (hydrophobic effect).

q: What property of carbon allows it to form long chains and rings?
o: Ability to form stable bonds with other elements
qs.e: Carbon's unique property of catenation allows it to form long chains and rings. Catenation is the ability of an atom to form strong covalent bonds with other atoms of the same element. Carbon exhibits exceptional catenation due to its small atomic size and high bond energy of C-C bonds (~348 kJ/mol). This enables carbon atoms to link together through single, double, or triple bonds (multiple bonds), forming stable extended structures like chains and rings. While carbon does form covalent bonds (option 4), this alone doesn't explain chain formation—many elements form covalent bonds but don't catenate well. Options 1 and 2 are too general; many elements form stable bonds or single bonds but cannot create complex chains like carbon.

☛ Carbon can form single (C-C), double (C=C), and triple (C≡C) bonds with itself, enabling diverse structures.
☛ The tetravalency of carbon (valency 4) allows it to bond with four other atoms, contributing to complex networks.
☛ Silicon also shows catenation but weaker than carbon due to larger atomic size and lower Si-Si bond energy (~222 kJ/mol).

☛ What enables carbon to form rings? → Ability to form multiple bonds and tetravalency

q: When a small piece of sodium metal is added to chlorine gas under controlled conditions, a vigorous reaction occurs producing sodium chloride. Which of the following statements best explains the reason for the stability of the product formed?
o: Sodium donates one electron to chlorine, forming oppositely charged ions held by strong electrostatic forces.
Both sodium and chlorine attain stability by forming a metallic lattice with delocalized electrons.
Sodium and chlorine share one electron each, forming a stable covalent bond.
Sodium gains one electron from chlorine, forming a neutral molecule through mutual sharing.
qs.e: The reaction between sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl₂) is a classic example of ionic bonding. Sodium (atomic number 11, electronic configuration 2,8,1) has one valence electron, while chlorine (atomic number 17, electronic configuration 2,8,7) needs one electron to achieve a stable octet. Sodium donates its single valence electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ cation and Cl⁻ anion. These oppositely charged ions are held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction (ionic bonds), forming a stable crystalline lattice of sodium chloride (NaCl). Option 2 is incorrect because NaCl forms an ionic lattice, not a metallic one with delocalized electrons. Option 3 is wrong as sodium and chlorine do not share electrons; the bond is ionic, not covalent. Option 4 is false because sodium loses an electron, not gains one, and the product is ionic, not a neutral molecule.

☛ In solid state, ionic compounds do not conduct electricity, but they do in molten state or aqueous solution.
☛ The formation of NaCl is an exothermic reaction, releasing about 411 kJ/mol of energy. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:

q: Which statement correctly describes an ion?

A charged atom or group of atoms
A compound formed by covalent bonds
A neutral atom formed by chemical bonding

Option 1 is incorrect because it describes a molecule of identical atoms (like O₂ or N₂), not necessarily charged. Option 3 is wrong as it refers to covalent compounds (e.g., H₂O), which are typically neutral molecules formed by electron sharing. qs.tag: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 : 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 2
q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about ‘nature of a carbon compound’?
o: Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called catenation.
Compounds of carbon having double or triple bonds between their carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
Compounds of carbon are only formed with oxygen.
Compounds of carbon, which are linked by only single bonds between the carbon atoms, are called saturated compounds.
qs.e: The incorrect statement is option 3 because carbon compounds are formed with many elements, not just oxygen. Carbon exhibits tetravalency (valency of 4) and can form covalent bonds with hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, halogens, sulfur, and other carbon atoms. This versatility leads to millions of organic compounds. Option 1 is correct: catenation is carbon's unique ability to form long chains with other carbon atoms. Option 2 is correct: unsaturated compounds contain double (C=C) or triple (C≡C) bonds between carbon atoms. Option 4 is correct: saturated compounds have only single bonds (C-C) between carbon atoms, like alkanes. Carbon's bonding diversity contradicts the limited scope in option 3.
qs.kf:
☛ Carbon forms more compounds than all other elements combined due to catenation and tetravalency.
☛ Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen (e.g., methane CH₄, ethene C₂H₄).
☛ Functional groups like -OH (alcohol), -COOH (carboxylic acid) determine organic compound properties.
☛ Carbon can form allotropes like diamond (tetrahedral network) and graphite (layered structure).
☛ Isomerism (same molecular formula, different structures) is common in carbon compounds. Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
☛ What is catenation? → Carbon's ability to form bonds with other carbon atoms into long chains.
☛ Define saturated hydrocarbon. → Hydrocarbons with only single bonds between carbon atoms (alkanes).
☛ What are unsaturated compounds? → Compounds with double or triple bonds between carbon atoms.
☛ Why does carbon form covalent bonds? → Due to its tetravalency and moderate electronegativity (2.55).

qs.tag: RRB Level 01 Stage I 29/12/2025 12:45 PM - 2:15 PM
q: What is the IUPAC rule for writing element symbols?
o: First letter uppercase, second lowercase (in case of two letters)
Two lowercase letters always used (in case of two letters)
Both letters always in uppercase form (in case of two letters)

Option 2 is incorrect because two lowercase letters are never used (e.g., 'na' would be wrong for Sodium). Option 3 is wrong as element symbols are not numeric codes. Option 4 is incorrect because both uppercase letters are not used (e.g., 'NA' would be incorrect for Sodium).

☛ IUPAC is the international authority on chemical nomenclature, terminology, and standardized measurement.
☛ Element symbols are derived from their English, Latin, or Greek names (e.g., Au from Latin 'Aurum' for Gold, K from Latin 'Kalium' for Potassium).
☛ Single-letter symbols are always uppercase (e.g., H for Hydrogen, O for Oxygen).
☛ This capitalization rule helps distinguish element symbols from other abbreviations in chemical formulas and equations.
☛ Some elements have symbols that don't match their English names directly, like Pb for Lead (from Latin 'Plumbum') and Ag for Silver (from Latin 'Argentum'). Important One-liners for Upcoming Exams:
